verdict.rationale: Galileo publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec with 202 /v2/ paths and a generated API reference with a per-endpoint "Try it" runner against the production API, plus path versioning and documented deprecations. The docs-origin OpenAPI probe 404s, but the spec is published at the API origin, so this is not a contradiction. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of driving the API end-to-end, and polish such as a standalone versioning/deprecation policy and proper spec metadata (it still carries the FastAPI default title and version).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Galileo publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document at its API origin (202 paths, all under /v2/)
The runner mounts client-side and executes against the production API with a real token.
the API is /v2 path-versioned, release notes record removals and method deprecations with migration guidance
